intent: Let the user move between the pages of one paged result set through links to each page.
typical_uses: Page numbers with previous and next links under a server-paged list, where every page has its own URL
A previous/next pair alone, with no page numbers

dont_use_when.situation: Loading more items into the same list, or infinite scroll
Paging the rows of a DataTable

instead.note: DataTable renders its own previous and next controls in its footer and owns the page state.

dont_use_when.situation: Showing where the current page sits in a hierarchy
Primary navigation between the application's top-level sections
Switching between sections of one page

invariants.text: Pagination renders a `nav` landmark named "pagination" through `aria-label`; the label is set ahead of the consumer's props, so an `aria-label` passed to Pagination replaces it.
The root is a full-width flex row that centers its content (pagination.module.css `.pagination`), so the page row sits in the middle of its container whatever the container's width.

a11y.by: pagination.test.tsx asserts getByRole('navigation', { name: 'pagination' }) resolves to a NAV element

good.title: Page numbers between previous and next links

bad.title: Links placed straight into the root
bad.why: Without PaginationContent and PaginationItem there is no list, so the links lose their list semantics and the spaced row pagination.module.css puts on `.content`.
